page: Microsoft Azure E32ds_v5 is a memory-optimized server instance belonging to the EDSv5 family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The server features 32 dedicated virtual CPUs, mapped from 16 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled at 2 threads per core. The base clock speed of the processor is 2.8 GHz, supported by 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. The hardware configuration includes 256.0 GB of RAM, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is provided via a bundled 1229 GB SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark evaluations show average performance across most standard compute and memory tasks. The stress-ng single-core CPU score is 1900.09, while the multi-core score reaches 31080.73. Memory bandwidth tests indicate a read-only small block cached speed of 1678.79 GB/sec, which drops to 143.87 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, and a large block write speed of 67.31 GB/sec. In database operations, the server achieves an average PassMark database score of 15337.83 and processes 31.13 million Redis SET operations per second. For language model workloads, text generation using a small 135M model is strong at 278.54 tokens per second, but performance drops to an average of 19.99 tokens per second for a medium 7B model, and prompt processing for a large 70B model is weak at 6.67 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E32ds_v5 offers a high memory-to-vCPU density and bundled local SSD storage, reducing the need for external storage attachments for temporary data. However, the lack of a dedicated GPU limits its utility for heavy machine learning training or large-scale LLM inference. The server is best suited for memory-intensive workloads, database hosting, software compilation, and static web serving.
